newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-VILLA WIN 1-0 TO DENT LIVERPOOL'S TITLE BID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VILLA WIN 1-0 TO DENT LIVERPOOL'S TITLE BID.

text.p: A late goal from midfielder Ian Taylor gave Aston Villa a 1-0 victory over Liverpool on Sunday which left leaders Manchester United breathing more easily at the top of the English premier league.
A tightly-contested match at Villa Park appeared to be heading for a 0-0 draw with both sides frustrated by a treacherous playing surface which cut up within minutes of kick-off.

But in the 83rd minute Irish international Andy Townsend swung in a cross from the Villa left and Taylor stole in unmarked at the back post to fire a half-volley past goalkeeper David James into the roof of the Liverpool net.
Liverpool surged forward in the remaining minutes and Steve McManaman and Robbie Fowler came close to grabbing late equalisers.

But Villa held on for a victory which put them back in the reckoning for a European qualification place and left defending champions United four points clear of Liverpool at the top of the table -- a significant lead heading into the final quarter of the season.
Alex Ferguson's side, who beat Coventry 3-1 on Saturday, have 57 points to Liverpool's 53. Both teams have played 28 matches.

Third-placed Arsenal have 51 points but have played a game more and Newcastle, with a game in hand on the leading pair, are a massive nine points behind United. Villa remain fifth with 46 points from 28 games.

"When the gap starts to open up it starts to look more of a daunting task but we have to stay with (United)," Liverpool manager Roy Evans said. "We've still got to play against them at home and we'll have to see how that goes.
Taylor's goal was the first Liverpool had conceded in the league since New Year's Day when they lost 1-0 at Chelsea.

More worrying for Liverpool will be the lack of form of striker Fowler, who missed a wonderful chance to put Liverpool ahead midway through the second half in another disappointing personal performance.
Villa's principal worry will be the state of their pitch.
"It looks like 200 elephants have been out there," television pundit and former Villa and Liverpool striker Dean Saunders observed at halftime.
